metadata.title: His-tagged Protein Purification by Ni-NTA Affinity Chromatography (Batch, Native Conditions)
metadata.purpose: Purify a 6xHis-tagged recombinant protein from a cleared E. coli lysate by binding it to Ni-NTA resin, washing away contaminants at low imidazole, and eluting the target with high imidazole under native (non-denaturing) conditions.
metadata.scope: Batch (gravity-flow) Ni-NTA purification of soluble 6xHis-tagged protein expressed in E. coli under native conditions, following QIAexpressionist Protocol 9 (cleared lysate) + Protocol 12 (batch purification). Denaturing purification (urea/GuHCl), FPLC/IMAC on a chromatography system, and periplasmic preparations are out of scope.
metadata.estimatedTime: ~3-4 h after cell harvest (30 min lysozyme + sonication + 20-30 min spin + 60 min binding + washes/elution)
beforeYouBegin: Confirm the target protein is soluble; even mostly-insoluble proteins may yield trace soluble material on Ni-NTA.
Prepare Lysis, Wash, and Elution buffers per the buffer table; all three differ only in imidazole (10 / 20 / 250 mM). Adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH.
Keep cells and lysate at 0-4 C throughout; consider adding 1 mM PMSF or other protease inhibitors on a case-by-case basis.
Ni-NTA resins are supplied as 50% slurries with a binding capacity of ~5-10 mg protein per mL resin.

materials.name: Lysis buffer (NPI-10)
materials.specification: 50 mM NaH2PO4, 300 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole; adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH
materials.rawText: Lysis buffer: 50 mM NaH2PO4 (6.90 g/L), 300 mM NaCl (17.54 g/L), 10 mM imidazole (0.68 g/L); adjust pH to 8.0 using NaOH

sourceReferences.excerpt: Lysis buffer (1 liter): 50 mM NaH2PO4 ... 300 mM NaCl ... 10 mM imidazole ... Adjust pH to 8.0 using NaOH.

materials.name: Wash buffer (NPI-20)
materials.specification: 50 mM NaH2PO4, 300 mM NaCl, 20 mM imidazole; adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH
materials.rawText: Wash buffer (1 liter): 50 mM NaH2PO4, 300 mM NaCl, 20 mM imidazole (1.36 g/L); Adjust pH to 8.0 using NaOH

sourceReferences.excerpt: Wash buffer (1 liter): ... 20 mM imidazole ... Adjust pH to 8.0 using NaOH.

materials.name: Elution buffer (NPI-250)
materials.specification: 50 mM NaH2PO4, 300 mM NaCl, 250 mM imidazole; adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH
materials.rawText: Elution buffer (1 liter): 50 mM NaH2PO4, 300 mM NaCl, 250 mM imidazole (17.00 g/L); Adjust pH to 8.0 using NaOH

sourceReferences.excerpt: Elution buffer (1 liter): ... 250 mM imidazole ... Adjust pH to 8.0 using NaOH.

materials.name: Ni-NTA agarose (50% slurry)
materials.workingConcentration: 1 mL of 50% slurry per 4 mL cleared lysate
materials.specification: Binding capacity ~5-10 mg protein/mL resin (0.3 umol/mL, 8.0 mg/mL for 6xHis-DHFR); supplied as 50% slurry
materials.rawText: The resins are supplied as 50% slurries. ... binding capacity ... between 5 and 10 mg/ml.

sourceReferences.excerpt: The resins are supplied as 50% slurries.

materials.name: Lysozyme
materials.specification: Added to resuspended cells for enzymatic lysis
materials.rawText: Add lysozyme to 1 mg/ml and incubate on ice for 30 min.

materials.name: RNase A
materials.specification: Optional; add if lysate is very viscous
materials.rawText: add RNase A (10 ug/ml) ... incubate on ice for 10-15 min

materials.name: DNase I
materials.specification: Optional; add if lysate is very viscous
materials.rawText: add ... DNase I (5 ug/ml) ... incubate on ice for 10-15 min

materials.name: 2x SDS-PAGE sample buffer
materials.specification: For preparing fraction aliquots (flow-through, wash, eluate) for SDS-PAGE analysis
materials.rawText: Add 5 ul 2x SDS-PAGE sample buffer to 5 ul supernatant and store at -20 C for SDS-PAGE analysis.

materials.name: PMSF (protease inhibitor)
materials.specification: Optional; case-by-case for native-condition lysis to limit degradation
materials.rawText: Addition of PMSF or other protease inhibitors may be helpful on a case-by-case basis

equipment.name: Ultrasonic cell disruptor (sonicator with microtip)
equipment.settings: Six 10 s bursts at 200-300 W with a 10 s cooling period between bursts; keep sample on ice

samples.name: E. coli cell pellet expressing 6xHis-tagged protein
samples.description: Frozen pellet from a 40-200 mL induced culture

samples.name: Cleared lysate (soluble fraction)
samples.description: Supernatant after sonication and 10,000 x g clarification

samples.name: Ni-NTA resin-bound 6xHis protein
samples.description: Target protein captured on Ni-NTA during batch binding

samples.name: Purified 6xHis-tagged protein eluate
samples.description: Protein released by 250 mM imidazole, collected in four 0.5 mL fractions

samples.name: Wash fractions
samples.description: 20 mM imidazole washes; saved for SDS-PAGE

tables.title: Ni-NTA native buffers (imidazole step gradient)
tables.note: All three buffers are identical except imidazole; the 10 -> 20 -> 250 mM step gradient gives binding, washing, and elution. Buffer names in parentheses follow the QIAGEN NPI convention.

steps.action: Thaw the cell pellet 15 min on ice and resuspend in Lysis buffer at 2-5 mL per gram wet weight.

parameters.rawText: Thaw the cell pellet for 15 min on ice
resuspend the cells in lysis buffer at 2-5 ml per gram wet weight

steps.criticalNotes: Lysis buffer contains 10 mM imidazole to suppress binding of untagged proteins. If the tagged protein does not bind, reduce imidazole to 1-5 mM; high-affinity tags tolerate up to 20 mM.

steps.action: Add lysozyme to 1 mg/mL and incubate on ice.
Sonicate on ice with a microtip.

parameters.rawText: 10 s cooling period between each burst

steps.criticalNotes: Keep the sample on ice; allow the cooling period between bursts to avoid heating.

steps.action: If the lysate is very viscous, add RNase A and DNase I and incubate on ice.
Centrifuge the lysate to pellet cell debris and save the supernatant (cleared lysate).
steps.criticalNotes: Insoluble target protein stays in the pellet; recover it only via denaturing purification if needed.

steps.action: Reserve an aliquot of cleared lysate in 2x SDS-PAGE sample buffer for gel analysis.

parameters.rawText: Add 5 ul 2x SDS-PAGE sample buffer to 5 ul supernatant

steps.action: Add 1 mL of 50% Ni-NTA slurry to 4 mL cleared lysate and mix gently by shaking at 4 C.

parameters.rawText: Add 1 ml of the 50% Ni-NTA slurry

sourceReferences.excerpt: Add 1 ml of the 50% Ni-NTA slurry to 4 ml cleared lysate and mix gently by shaking (200 rpm on a rotary shaker) at 4 C for 60 min.

steps.action: Load the lysate-Ni-NTA mixture into a column with the bottom outlet capped.
Remove the bottom cap and collect the flow-through; save it for SDS-PAGE.
Wash twice with 4 mL Wash buffer (20 mM imidazole); collect wash fractions for SDS-PAGE.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Wash twice with 4 ml wash buffer; collect wash fractions for SDS-PAGE analysis.

steps.action: Elute the target protein 4 times with 0.5 mL Elution buffer (250 mM imidazole), collecting each in a separate tube; analyze by SDS-PAGE.
steps.expectedResult: 6xHis-tagged protein released in the eluate; typically most concentrated in the first 1-2 fractions.
steps.criticalNotes: Buffers may be modified (e.g. 0.1% Tween, 5-10 mM beta-ME, 1 mM PMSF, higher NaCl or glycerol) to suit the protein.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Elute the protein 4 times with 0.5 ml elution buffer. Collect the eluate in four tubes and analyze by SDS-PAGE.

controls.name: Fraction ladder for SDS-PAGE
controls.description: Run cleared lysate, flow-through, wash, and eluate fractions side by side to assess capture, wash stringency, and purity.

controls.name: Uninduced-culture control
controls.description: Lysate from an uninduced culture confirms the eluted band is the induced 6xHis-tagged protein.

expectedOutputs: Purified 6xHis-tagged protein in the 250 mM imidazole elution fractions.
SDS-PAGE showing enrichment of the target band from lysate -> flow-through -> wash -> eluate.
Saved flow-through and wash fractions documenting binding/wash performance.

troubleshooting.cause: Imidazole in lysis buffer too high; protein insoluble; overloaded resin
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce lysis-buffer imidazole to 1-5 mM; verify solubility; add more resin (capacity 5-10 mg/mL)

troubleshooting.problem: Low purity / contaminating bands in eluate
troubleshooting.solution: Increase imidazole in wash buffer (up to ~20 mM) or add more wash steps
Elute with a higher imidazole step or a pH step-gradient

safety: Imidazole is an irritant; wear gloves and eye protection.
PMSF is toxic and corrosive; prepare and handle with care.
Follow institutional rules for the E. coli expression host and the recombinant protein.
limitations: Native-conditions batch protocol; recovers only soluble target. Resin lot, exact culture size, and protein-specific imidazole optimum are not fixed here. Insoluble protein requires a separate denaturing (urea/GuHCl) purification.
